subproblems.title: An embedded submanifold is Borel and meets small closed balls in compact sets
subproblems.statement: Let P, r, d ∈ ℕ and M ⊆ ℝ^P with IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M, i.e. every y ∈ M has open sets V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W and a map ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P that is C^r on V and injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(v) injective for v ∈ V. Then (a) M is a (Borel) measurable subset of ℝ^P, and (b) every y ∈ M has some ε > 0 such that M ∩ closedBall(y, ε) is compact.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P r d : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M → MeasurableSet M ∧ ∀ y ∈ M, ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ IsCompact (M ∩ closedBall y ε)

Use in the selected node: step 2 of the supplied proof (local compactness of M near y, and M Borel). The selected node's assembly applies part (b) at y to get ε > 0 with M ∩ closedBall(y, ε) compact, chooses ρ := min(ρ₀, ε), and uses that this compact (hence closed) set gives closure(M) ∩ B_ε(y) ⊆ M. The sibling submanifold_subset_support uses part (a) (MeasurableSet M) for the integrals over M. The numbered proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied natural-language proof, copied verbatim (its Lean reference block is omitted).

Accepted proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied parent proof ("M ∩ closedBall y (2ρ₁) = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(closedBall y (2ρ₁))) is compact"), together with the measurability of M that the parent needs for the integrals ∫_M. Only continuity of ψ on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M and the properness of the charts are used.
1. (Compact slices of a chart.) Let y ∈ M and let (V, W, ψ) be a chart at y given by IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M. Claim: for every compact K ⊆ W the set M ∩ K is compact. First, M ∩ K = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K)). Indeed, if x ∈ M ∩ K then x ∈ W because K ⊆ W, so x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V); write x = ψ(v) with v ∈ V, and then v ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K). Conversely, for v ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) we have ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ M and ψ(v) ∈ K. Next, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact by the properness clause of the chart, and ψ is continuous on V (a C^r map on V is continuous there, for every r ≥ 0), hence continuous on V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K). The continuous image of a compact set is compact, so M ∩ K is compact.
2. (Part (b).) W is open and y ∈ W, so there is r' > 0 with ball(y, r') ⊆ W. Put ε := r'/2 > 0. Then closedBall(y, ε) ⊆ ball(y, r') ⊆ W, and closedBall(y, ε) is compact because ℝ^P is a proper metric space. By step 1, M ∩ closedBall(y, ε) is compact.
3. (An open set containing M.) For each y ∈ M choose a chart (V_y, W_y, ψ_y) at y, and let O := ⋃_{y ∈ M} W_y. O is open, being a union of open sets, and M ⊆ O because y ∈ W_y.
4. (M = O ∩ closure(M).) The inclusion M ⊆ O ∩ closure(M) is clear from step 3. Conversely, let p ∈ O ∩ closure(M). Pick y ∈ M with p ∈ W_y and r' > 0 with ball(p, r') ⊆ W_y. The set C := M ∩ closedBall(p, r'/2) is compact by step 1 (closedBall(p, r'/2) is compact and contained in ball(p, r') ⊆ W_y), hence closed. Since ball(p, r'/2) is open, ball(p, r'/2) ∩ closure(M) ⊆ closure(ball(p, r'/2) ∩ M), and p belongs to the left-hand side. Hence p ∈ closure(ball(p, r'/2) ∩ M) ⊆ closure(C) = C ⊆ M.
5. (Part (a).) By step 4, M is the intersection of the open set O and the closed set closure(M). Open and closed sets are Borel, so M is measurable.
proof_key_steps: Chart slices: for compact K ⊆ W, M ∩ K = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K)) is compact by properness and continuity of ψ on V.
A closed ball around y inside the chart domain W meets M in a compact set.
With O the union of the chart domains, M = O ∩ closure(M), so M is Borel.

subproblems.title: An embedded C¹ n-submanifold has n-dimensional density one at each of its points
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ ℝ^P satisfy IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M, and let z ∈ M. Then Hⁿ(M ∩ B_s(z))/(ω_n sⁿ) → 1 as s ↓ 0, computed in [0, ∞], where Hⁿ = μHE[n], B_s(z) is the open ball, and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M → z ∈ M → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => μHE[n] (M ∩ ball z s) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (s ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)

Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node; its own prerequisites (Submission.dimred_rpd_near_isometric_chart and Submission.dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure, called the sibling lemmas near_isometric_chart and bilipschitz_measure in the proof below, and Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity behind the former) are already discharged in that accepted checkpoint. The numbered proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied natural-language proof, copied verbatim (its Lean reference block is omitted).

Accepted proof:
Source: step 4 of the supplied parent proof ("a C¹ embedded submanifold has H^n-density 1 at each of its points": H^n(M ∩ B_s(z)) = ω_n s^n(1 + o(1)) as s ↓ 0). The supplied graph and area-formula computation is replaced by a bi-Lipschitz squeeze. It needs neither the inverse function theorem nor the area formula, and n = 0 needs no separate treatment.
Notation. ω_n := unitBallVolume n. It lies in (0, ∞) because the unit ball of ℝ^n is nonempty, open and bounded (measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top). For r > 0, Lⁿ(B_r(0)) = rⁿ·ω_n (Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos, with finrank ℝ^n = n). Put R(s) := Hⁿ(M ∩ B_s(z))/(ω_n·sⁿ) for s > 0.
1. (Two-sided bounds for a fixed ε ∈ (0, 1).) By the sibling lemma near_isometric_chart, choose χ : ℝ^n → ℝ^P and δ, δ' > 0 such that:
 - χ(0) = z;
 - (1 − ε)|a − b| ≤ |χ(a) − χ(b)| ≤ (1 + ε)|a − b| for all a, b ∈ B_δ(0);
 - χ(B_δ(0)) ⊆ M;
 - M ∩ B_{δ'}(z) ⊆ χ(B_δ(0)).
 Let 0 < s < min(δ', (1 − ε)δ), and put r₁ := s/(1 + ε) and r₂ := s/(1 − ε). Then 0 < r₁ ≤ r₂ < δ.
 (a) χ(B_{r₁}(0)) ⊆ M ∩ B_s(z). For |w| < r₁ we have χ(w) ∈ M and |χ(w) − z| = |χ(w) − χ(0)| ≤ (1 + ε)|w| < (1 + ε)r₁ = s.
 (b) M ∩ B_s(z) ⊆ χ(B_{r₂}(0)). Let x ∈ M ∩ B_s(z). Then x ∈ M ∩ B_{δ'}(z), so x = χ(w) with |w| < δ. Hence (1 − ε)|w| ≤ |χ(w) − χ(0)| = |x − z| < s, that is, |w| < r₂.
 (c) Apply the sibling lemma bilipschitz_measure with c₁ = 1 − ε and c₂ = 1 + ε, to E = B_{r₁}(0) and to E = B_{r₂}(0). Both are subsets of B_δ(0), where the bi-Lipschitz bounds hold. With (a), (b) and monotonicity of Hⁿ:
 Hⁿ(M ∩ B_s(z)) ≥ Hⁿ(χ(B_{r₁}(0))) ≥ (1 − ε)ⁿ r₁ⁿ ω_n = ((1 − ε)/(1 + ε))ⁿ sⁿ ω_n,
 Hⁿ(M ∩ B_s(z)) ≤ Hⁿ(χ(B_{r₂}(0))) ≤ (1 + ε)ⁿ r₂ⁿ ω_n = ((1 + ε)/(1 − ε))ⁿ sⁿ ω_n.
 Dividing by ω_n sⁿ ∈ (0, ∞) gives ((1 − ε)/(1 + ε))ⁿ ≤ R(s) ≤ ((1 + ε)/(1 − ε))ⁿ for all s ∈ (0, min(δ', (1 − ε)δ)).
2. (Limit.) The real functions ε ↦ ((1 − ε)/(1 + ε))ⁿ and ε ↦ ((1 + ε)/(1 − ε))ⁿ are continuous at 0 with value 1, so their images under ofReal tend to 1 as ε → 0.
 - Given a < 1, choose ε ∈ (0, 1) with ofReal(((1 − ε)/(1 + ε))ⁿ) > a. By step 1, a < R(s) for all sufficiently small s > 0.
 - Given b > 1, choose ε ∈ (0, 1) with ofReal(((1 + ε)/(1 − ε))ⁿ) < b. By step 1, R(s) < b for all sufficiently small s > 0.
 Hence R(s) → 1 as s ↓ 0 (order characterization of convergence in [0, ∞], tendsto_order).

subproblems.title: Unit orientations of n-planes are nonzero n-vectors of operator norm at most one
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P n, i.e. a continuous linear functional on the normed space Λ^n(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P (with Mathlib's operator norm). Let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P. Suppose ξ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q): there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P spanning Q such that either ξ(α) = α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every α. Then ξ ≠ 0 and ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 (operator norm on (Λ^n)*).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → ξ ≠ 0 ∧ ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1

Use in the selected node: step 5(a) of the supplied proof, i.e. steps 0(ii), 2 and 8(c) of the sibling submanifold_subset_support: ξ(x) ≠ 0 yields a covector α with ξ(x)(α) = 1, and ‖ξ(z)‖ ≤ 1 on M bounds the integrand by ‖α‖. The numbered proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied natural-language proof, copied verbatim (its Lean reference block is omitted).

Accepted proof:
Source: parent proof steps 1(b)–(c) (Simon Ch. 6, 1.1 and 1.7: a unit orientation is ξ = ±τ_1∧⋯∧τ_n for an orthonormal basis τ of the plane).
Notation: Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖α‖ = inf{C ≥ 0 : |α(w)| ≤ C∏_i‖w_i‖ for all w}, and Λ_n = MultiVector P n = (Λ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ) carries its operator norm. The hypothesis that τ spans Q is not used.

1. Unpacking. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q there are a family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) and a sign ε ∈ {1, −1} such that ξ(α) = ε·α(τ) for every α ∈ Λ^n, where α(τ) := α(τ_1,…,τ_n). The family is orthonormal: ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i and ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = 0 for i ≠ j. The two branches of the disjunction are ε = 1 and ε = −1.

2. Norm bound. Let α ∈ Λ^n. By the operator-norm inequality for continuous multilinear maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) and ‖τ_i‖ = 1,
 |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_{i=1}^n ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖.
 So |ξ(α)| ≤ 1·‖α‖ for all α, and therefore ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound with the constant 1 ≥ 0).

3. A test covector. Put m(w_1,…,w_n) := ∏_{i=1}^n ⟨τ_i, w_i⟩. Let δ := Alt(m) be its alternatization (ContinuousMultilinearMap.alternatization). Then δ is a continuous alternating n-linear form, i.e. δ ∈ Λ^n, and by alternatization_apply_apply

4. δ(τ) = 1. We have δ(τ) = Σ_σ sign(σ) ∏_i ⟨τ_i, τ_{σ(i)}⟩.
 - If σ ≠ id, choose i with σ(i) ≠ i. Orthonormality gives ⟨τ_i, τ_{σ(i)}⟩ = 0, so that product is 0 (Finset.prod_eq_zero).

 Hence δ(τ) = 1 (Finset.sum_eq_single). This includes n = 0, where S_0 = {id} and the empty product is 1.

5. Nonvanishing. ξ(δ) = ε·δ(τ) = ε ∈ {1, −1}, so ξ(δ) ≠ 0. If ξ were 0 we would have ξ(δ) = 0. Hence ξ ≠ 0.

6. Steps 2 and 5 give ξ ≠ 0 ∧ ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1.

subproblems.title: The support of a current equal to m[[M]] on an open set G lies, inside G, in the closure of M
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, G, M ⊆ ℝ^P be sets, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), m ∈ ℤ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n). Assume G is open, G ⊆ U, and T(ω) = m·∫_M ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) (Hⁿ := μHE[n]) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ G. Then spt T ∩ G ⊆ closure(M), where spt T = T.support = U ∖ zeroRegion T (Simon 6.2.11).

Source: step 4 of the supplied proof of the selected node ("spt T ∩ B_ρ(y) ⊆ M": a point that has a ball missing M lies in the zero region, because every test form supported in that ball vanishes on M). Here it is stated for an arbitrary open set G ⊆ U on which T = m[[M]], with conclusion closure(M). No submanifold, orientation or measure hypothesis is needed. The selected node applies it with G = B_{ρ₀}(y), and then uses local compactness of M near y to replace closure(M) by M.
Conventions. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and a set W, "T vanishes on W" (T.VanishesOn W) means T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. zeroRegion T is the union of all open sets W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and T vanishing on W, and spt T = T.support = U ∖ zeroRegion T (SimonGMT Chapter06/CurrentLocalEquality.lean; Simon 6.2.11).
1. Let x ∈ spt T ∩ G. Then x ∈ U, x ∉ zeroRegion T and x ∈ G. Suppose, for a contradiction, that x ∉ closure(M).
2. (A ball missing M.) The set G ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ closure(M)) is open, as the intersection of the open set G with the complement of the closed set closure(M), and it contains x. Hence there is ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ G and B_ε(x) ∩ closure(M) = ∅. In particular no point of M lies in B_ε(x).
3. (The set W.) Put W := B_{ε/2}(x). Then W is open and x ∈ W. Moreover closure(W) ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall). The closed ball is compact because ℝ^P is a proper metric space, so its closed subset closure(W) is compact. Finally closure(W) ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ G ⊆ U, since ε/2 < ε.
4. (T vanishes on W.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Since W ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ G, the hypothesis gives T(ω) = m·∫_M ξ(z)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z). Let z ∈ M. By step 2, z ∉ B_ε(x), so z ∉ W ⊇ tsupport ω. Hence ω(z) = 0, since a function vanishes outside its topological support (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Then ξ(z)(ω(z)) = ξ(z)(0) = 0 because ξ(z) is linear. So the integrand vanishes at every point of M, and ∫_M ξ(z)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero, which needs no measurability). Therefore T(ω) = m·0 = 0.
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 4, W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion T, and x ∈ W. Hence x ∈ zeroRegion T, contradicting step 1. Therefore x ∈ closure(M). Since x ∈ spt T ∩ G was arbitrary, spt T ∩ G ⊆ closure(M). ∎

Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected node (M ∩ B_ρ(y) ⊆ spt T, the bump-form argument (a)–(g)). Here it is stated for an arbitrary open set G ⊆ U on which T = m[[M]], with both B_ρ(y) and B_{ρ₀}(y) of the supplied proof replaced by G. The supplied proof takes some facts from its steps 2–3; here they are obtained as follows. M is Borel by the sibling embedded_locally_closed. Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for the compact ball K ⊆ G is a hypothesis. The integrand is integrable because it is bounded by ‖α‖ on a set of finite measure, so compactness of M ∩ K is not needed.
Conventions. Hⁿ := μHE[n], ω_n := unitBallVolume n, B_r(x) := ball x r. For T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), "T vanishes on W" means T(ω) = 0 for each ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. zeroRegion T is the union of the open sets W with closure(W) compact and closure(W) ⊆ U on which T vanishes, and spt T = T.support = U ∖ zeroRegion T (Simon 6.2.11). Λⁿ = Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm of continuous alternating maps, and Λ_n = MultiVector P n = (Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ) its operator norm, so |ξ(z)(β)| ≤ ‖ξ(z)‖·‖β‖.
0. (Facts about M and ξ.)
 (i) By the sibling embedded_locally_closed (Submission.dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed with r = 1, d = n), M is a measurable set.
 (ii) By IsOrientation n M ξ, ξ is continuous on M, and for every z ∈ M there is a subspace Q_z with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(z)) Q_z. So by the sibling unit_orientation_bounds (Submission.imsupp_unit_orientation_ne_zero_norm_le_one), ξ(z) ≠ 0 and ‖ξ(z)‖ ≤ 1 for every z ∈ M.
1. (Setting up the contradiction.) Let x ∈ M ∩ G. Then x ∈ U because G ⊆ U, so it remains to show x ∉ zeroRegion T. Suppose instead that x ∈ zeroRegion T. Then x ∈ W for some open set W (with closure(W) compact and contained in U) on which T vanishes.
2. (A covector α with ξ(x)(α) = 1.) By step 0(ii), ξ(x) ≠ 0, so there is α₀ ∈ Λⁿ with ξ(x)(α₀) ≠ 0; otherwise ξ(x) would be the zero functional. Put α := ξ(x)(α₀)⁻¹·α₀. By linearity, ξ(x)(α) = ξ(x)(α₀)⁻¹·ξ(x)(α₀) = 1.
3. (Continuity.) The function z ↦ ξ(z)(α) is continuous on M: ξ is continuous on M, and evaluating a continuous linear map at the fixed covector α is continuous (ContinuousOn.clm_apply with a constant). Since ξ(x)(α) = 1, there is ε₁ > 0 such that |ξ(z)(α) − 1| < 1/2, hence ξ(z)(α) > 1/2, for every z ∈ M with |z − x| < ε₁.
4. (Radius.) W ∩ G is open and contains x, so there is r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ W ∩ G. Put ε := min(r, ε₁) > 0. Then ε ≤ ε₁ and closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ B_r(x) ⊆ W ∩ G.
5. (The bump form.) Let g be Mathlib's smooth bump function centred at x with inner radius ε/4 and outer radius ε/2 (a ContDiffBump x with rIn = ε/4 and rOut = ε/2; note 0 < ε/4 < ε/2). It has these properties:
 - g is C^∞ and 0 ≤ g ≤ 1;
 - g = 1 on closedBall(x, ε/4) (one_of_mem_closedBall);
 - tsupport g = closedBall(x, ε/2) (tsupport_eq), so g(z) = 0 for z ∉ closedBall(x, ε/2);
 - g has compact support.
 Define the n-form ω(z) := g(z)·α. It is C^∞ as the product of the smooth function g and the constant α. It has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g = closedBall(x, ε/2) (tsupport_smul_subset_left). Since closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ W ∩ G ⊆ U, we get ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), i.e. ω is a TestFormOn U n.
6. (T(ω) = 0.) tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ W and T vanishes on W, so T(ω) = 0.
7. (T(ω) as an integral.) tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ G, so the representation hypothesis gives T(ω) = m·∫_M h dHⁿ with h(z) := ξ(z)(ω(z)). By linearity of ξ(z), h(z) = ξ(z)(g(z)·α) = g(z)·ξ(z)(α).
8. (Properties of h.) Let μ := Hⁿ⌞M (μHE[n].restrict M) and K := closedBall(x, ε/2).
 (a) h is continuous on M, as the product of the continuous g and the function of step 3. Since M is measurable (step 0(i)), h is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable).
 (b) h(z) = 0 for z ∉ K, because g(z) = 0 there.
 (c) For z ∈ M, |h(z)| = |g(z)|·|ξ(z)(α)| ≤ 1·‖ξ(z)‖·‖α‖ ≤ ‖α‖, using 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and step 0(ii). Since μ-almost every point lies in M, |h| ≤ ‖α‖ μ-a.e.
 (d) K is compact and K ⊆ G, so Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ by hypothesis. Since K is measurable, μ(K) = Hⁿ(K ∩ M) < ∞.
 (e) (Integrability.) By (a), (c) and (d), h is integrable on K with respect to μ, being a bounded a.e.-strongly measurable function on a set of finite measure (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). By (b), h vanishes off K, so h is μ-integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero).
 (f) (Nonnegativity.) h ≥ 0 μ-a.e. Let z ∈ M. If z ∈ K, then |z − x| ≤ ε/2 < ε ≤ ε₁, so ξ(z)(α) > 1/2 > 0 by step 3; with g(z) ≥ 0 this gives h(z) ≥ 0. If z ∉ K, then h(z) = 0 by (b).
 (g) (Where h is positive.) Let z ∈ M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x). Then z ∈ closedBall(x, ε/4), so g(z) = 1. Also |z − x| < ε/4 < ε₁, so h(z) = ξ(z)(α) > 1/2 > 0. Hence M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x) ⊆ {h ≠ 0} ∩ M.
9. (M has positive measure near x.) We claim Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) > 0. Suppose instead that Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) = 0. For every s ∈ (0, ε/4), monotonicity gives Hⁿ(M ∩ B_s(x)) = 0, so Hⁿ(M ∩ B_s(x))/(ω_n sⁿ) = 0, since in [0, ∞] zero divided by anything is zero. So this ratio is eventually 0 as s ↓ 0, and it tends to 0. But M is an embedded C¹ n-submanifold and x ∈ M, so by the sibling submanifold_density_one (Submission.dimred_rpd_submanifold_density_one) the same ratio tends to 1 as s ↓ 0. The filter s ↓ 0 (𝓝[>] 0) is nontrivial and limits in [0, ∞] are unique, so 1 = 0, which is absurd.
10. (The integral is positive.) For a μ-integrable function that is ≥ 0 μ-a.e., ∫ h dμ > 0 if and only if μ({h ≠ 0}) > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae, applicable by 8(e) and 8(f)). By 8(g), step 9 and Measure.le_restrict_apply, μ({h ≠ 0}) ≥ Hⁿ({h ≠ 0} ∩ M) ≥ Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) > 0. Hence ∫_M h dHⁿ = ∫ h dμ > 0. This is the supplied proof's bound ∫_M h dHⁿ ≥ ∫_{M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)} h dHⁿ ≥ ½·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) > 0, stated as a positivity criterion.
11. (Contradiction.) By steps 6 and 7, 0 = T(ω) = m·∫_M h dHⁿ. But m ≠ 0, so (m : ℝ) ≠ 0, and ∫_M h dHⁿ > 0 by step 10, so the product is nonzero. This contradiction shows x ∉ zeroRegion T, hence x ∈ U ∖ zeroRegion T = spt T. Since x ∈ M ∩ G was arbitrary, M ∩ G ⊆ spt T. ∎
